title: Side-Effecting Initialization inside Functional Subroutines
pattern: A domain-logic computation method (e.g., `compute_marketing_expense`) is implicitly tasked with initializing shared class-level/global data structures that other sibling routines depend on.
why_bad: Violates the single-responsibility principle. The method names suggest they are coordinate sibling computations, but one of them has a hidden temporal priority because of its initialization side effect.
detection: One sibling method initializes a shared mutable field while other sibling methods read that field and panic/fail if it is uninitialized.
counterexample: Two independent functions that both read/write to a pre-initialized data structure without depending on a specific execution order.
fix: Extract the shared initialization code into an explicit initialization routine (e.g., `initialize_expense_data()`) and call it independently during lifecycle setup.
